title: Algebraic inductive step for the Bonami lemma
statement:
Fix a natural number $m$, and let $a, b, B, C$ be nonnegative real numbers and $A$ a real number satisfying $A \le 9^{m+1} a^2$, $B \le 9^m b^2$, and $C^2 \le A B$. Then
\[
A + 6C + B \le 9^{m+1}\,(a+b)^2.
\]
replaced:
The key algebraic inequality driving the inductive step of the Bonami lemma: for
$a, b, A, B, C \ge 0$ (with $a, b, B, C$ nonnegative) satisfying
$A \le 9^{m+1} a^2$, $B \le 9^m b^2$, and $C^2 \le A\cdot B$, one has
\[
A + 6C + B \le 9^{m+1}\,(a+b)^2.
\]
